# beowulf-fitt-42 — crux notes (drafter)

Guesses and disputed readings, with what units.json chose.

- 3074–3075 (unit "Næs hē goldhwæte"): `goldhwæte` has a wrong-looking ending; read as "gold-keen", "he was not gold-keen; more readily had he earlier beheld the owner's favour". Who "the owner" is (God, or the hoard's owner) is unknown. Lawrence's `næfne` + comma reading (curse conditional on the owner's leave) is given in the note. Disputed.
- 3060 `fēara sumne`: "one of the few"; who the few are is a guess (rare, outstanding men; Beowulf).
- 3062–3065 `Wundur hwār`: "a wonder where" read as "it is a mystery where".
- 3072 `hergum geheaðerod`: "shut up in heathen shrines" (hearg + heaþor); guess.
- 3084 `healdon` (MS heoldon): taken as an infinitive after `lēte`, with the dragon as subject; alternatives (`hēoldon` "we kept", `hēold on`) listed in the note.
- 3085 `gifeðe`: taken as a noun "lot, fate"; guess.
- 3086 `[mannan]`: Klaeber's fill, not credited in the apparatus; Grundtvig `[þēoden]`, others `[þēodcyning]`.
- 3095 `gomol on gehðo`: `gehðo` "sorrow, care"; guess.
- 3107 `geferian`: bare infinitive read as continuing `uton` of 3101.
- 3112 `gōdum tōgēnes`: "towards the good one", taken as Beowulf; plural possible.
- 3115 `weaxan wonna lēg`: restored words in round brackets; Trautmann `wēstan`.
- 3118–3119 `sceft nytte hēold … flāne fullēode`: `fullēode` taken as "followed up" (fullgān); guess.
- 3129 `lȳt ǣnig mearn`: `mearn` taken as "hesitated"; `lǣne licgan` "lying fleeting/ownerless"; both guesses.
- 3132 `wēg`: taken as a spelling of `wæg` "wave"; alternative "take (its) way".
- 3134 `Þā` (MS þ only): rendered "Then"; `þǣr`, `þon` are the alternatives.
- 3135 `æþeling boren`: MS `æþelinge`; Klaeber drops the ending; no word for "and" (Barnouw, Trautmann `[ond]`).
- 3136 `hilde[rinc]`: MS blank, possibly an erased letter; `-rinc` is an editor's fill.
- 3067 `seolfa`: taken as a variant of `sylfa`; guess.
- 3059 `gehȳdde`: the hider is taken as the dragon; Bugge, Holthausen `gehȳðde` would make it the thief.
